rationale:
Two sibling completion gates hold OPPOSITE policies on the same question — 'the gate cannot read what it was asked to judge'. Gate 2 (registered verifiers) fails CLOSED by OWNER RULING of 2026-08-08 (RFC_017): 'I could not check' is not 'I checked and it is fixed'. Its own code deliberately routes an unparseable spec down that branch, saying exemption 'would leave a second silent completion path behind the one RFC_017 closed'. Gate 1b (noChangeGates, written 2026-08-13, five days AFTER that ruling) is exactly such a path: when none of an opted-in type's declared counters resolve, it completes the item and writes a log row.

Why that is not merely untidy: the roster is OPT-IN, and an entry is an assertion WITH A MEASUREMENT that for THIS type a zero-change run cannot be a repair. An unreadable payload silently waived the one thing the type's owners had established — and it waives it by default for every future repair type somebody adds.

MEASURED, and it is stronger than 'failed to grade': of the 11 NO_CHANGE_GATE_UNREADABLE_RESULT rows (agent_error_log, 2026-08-14 -> 08-17), FIVE are items this gate had ALREADY BLOCKED one attempt earlier — status complete, attempt_count 1, with the block sentence still in site_work_items.error (completion never clears that column, which is why the sequence is still legible): 0ceacd8f, 9ae28ee3, f65a1834, f4003032, a2ef2613. The gate refused, the item retried, the retry returned an unreadable payload, and the abstain arm completed it. The arm REVERSED the gate's own refusal.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING, because reviewers should not have to find it. (1) The hole is LATENT, not leaking: 7 of the 11 payloads were a SPAWN RECORD, which is bugs_closed/287 — fixed and live on v1.0.1307 (2026-08-17 17:05Z), after which that shape appears 0 times in 1,880 fleet completions against 939 before. (2) This will be UNEXERCISED on arrival: zero dark_section_audit rows have been touched since that roll (against 1,862 fleet completions), and both carriers that dispatch the type are enabled=false. Filings do continue (7 on 08-14, 5 on 08-15, 2 on 08-17), so it is not a dead type. (3) The cost of a refusal is REAL and is not tidied up: the row burns max_attempts and waits at failed for a human, because WII-018's silence retraction has NEVER run (0 rows carry result.retraction; the design carrier is off since 08-11). That is the cost the owner knowingly accepted for RFC_017. The refuse->attempts->retraction valve IS proven once, on empty_section 8ab3a32b (gate errored 08-09, detector retracted it 08-14), so the architecture works — it is simply not switched on for this producer.

SCOPE: I judge this a council-gate change, not architecture-scope, and the argument is explicit. Per the 2026-07-29 ruling 1, an RFC is owed when the shared mechanism's GUARANTEE changes: for every item_type absent from the roster this is byte-identical (a map miss — mutation M6 is the containment control), and for roster types the guarantee was always 'per-type declared judgement with a measured licence' — this adds a declared axis and changes behaviour only for the one entry edited, in the same commit, with its measurement. No fleet-wide default flips, which is what made RFC_017 itself architecture-scope. Per the 2026-08-02 RFC_010 narrowing 2, the new authority ships as an OPT-IN FIELD with the unsafe default OFF. Per the 2026-08-11 RFC_022 narrowing, conditions (1) opt-in and (2) unsafe-default-OFF hold but (3) fails — dark_section_audit names the field in this same commit — so I do not claim that safe harbour; losing it returns the question to ruling 1 above. Precedent on the point: WII-013's Grades shipped with a live consumer naming it in the same commit and went through this gate; WII-017 — this very roster's first entry, a NEW blocking outcome on the same shared path — also went through this gate and was APPROVED at round 2.

WHICH SIDE IS UNSAFE, since the answer is not symmetric: REFUSING is new blocking authority on a shared completion path whose measured failure mode was exactly shape drift, so it must cost a declared line carrying a licence. ABSTAINING is the WII-001 false green for a repair type. Neither may be an author-time silent default — which is what the three-valued type buys: the zero value is NOT a policy (it abstains at runtime AND the roster test refuses to let it ship).

CONSUMERS ENUMERATED, not asserted: `grep -rn OnUnreadable platform/` returns 0 outside this change. The only cross-cutting effect is that site_work_items.result->'_verification'->>'status' gains a FIFTH value, handler_result_unreadable — WII-011's landmine about reading that column is amended in the same commit, and blockedCompletionReason gives the value its own sentence and reason code because that function's whole history is a message recording a finding the verifier never made. The 213 and 287 lanes are the other consumers of the abstain stream and are told: post-287 a fresh NO_CHANGE_GATE_UNREADABLE_RESULT row on this type is a signal, not the expected background WII-017 describes.

REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, and why it is not merely more expensive: bugs_open/302's own re-ordered working candidate is gate-2 artefact verifiers for the design-repair family. verifier_coverage_test.go — the guard that exists so these gaps are decisions rather than accidents — ALREADY classifies that family with reasons: dark_section_audit and contrast_failure as needing a browser (an outbound probe on the completion path, the standing objection recorded in three places), and needs_design_review / spacing_fix / responsive_fix as catJudgement, 'an LLM design opinion; nothing to re-run'. And the mandated producer split (archive-inclusive, so a lifetime count rather than the 7-day window site_work_items alone gives) says needs_design_review has FOUR producers over 1,296 rows — one verifier there is bugs_closed/213's defect exactly. That route needs a Grades remit test per type on top, and an argument against a specific recorded reason, which I do not have.

plan.summary: Make gate 1b's unreadable-payload outcome a PER-TYPE DECLARATION whose zero value is not a policy, set it to REFUSE for the one live roster entry with the measurement that licenses it, give the refusal its own _verification status and operator message, and force every future roster entry to declare — extending the two guards that already exist rather than adding new mechanisms.

edits.rationale: Adds the per-type declaration and collapses the return contract. The tri-state's zero value (unreadableUndeclared) is deliberately NOT a policy: it abstains at runtime so an entry written by somebody who never read the comment cannot start blocking completions, and the roster test refuses to let it ship. noChangeOutcome replaces (detail, noChange, unknownShape) — that triple could express 'blocked AND unknown shape', a contradictory state the caller previously had to be defended against by a test rather than being unable to occur.
edits.sketch:
+type unreadableOutcome int
+const (
+	unreadableUndeclared unreadableOutcome = iota // zero value: NOT a policy
+	unreadableAbstains                            // pre-2026-08-18 behaviour, now a stated choice
+	unreadableRefuses                             // will not certify what it cannot read
+)
+type noChangeOutcome int
+const ( noChangePass noChangeOutcome = iota; noChangeBlocked; noChangeUnreadableBlocked; noChangeUnreadableAbstained )
 type noChangeRule struct {
 	Why          string
 	CounterPaths []string
+	OnUnreadable  unreadableOutcome
+	UnreadableWhy string   // required for unreadableRefuses (roster test)
 }

edits.rationale: The shape text is built identically either way, because naming what WAS in the payload is the useful half of the observation in both directions. Only the verdict differs, and it comes from the type's own declaration rather than from this function's assumption. The default arm covers BOTH unreadableAbstains and the undeclared zero value — that is the safety property, not laziness.

The only live roster entry opts in to refusal, with the measurement in UnreadableWhy — a SEPARATE field from Why on purpose: Why licenses 'zero counters cannot be a repair' (a claim about the handler's transform), this licenses 'a payload I cannot read cannot be a repair either' (a claim about the payloads the type actually receives). Different question, different evidence.

+			"abstain-completions 2026-08-14→08-17, 7 were a SPAWN RECORD (bugs_closed/287, fixed and rolled on "+
+			"v1.0.1307), 3 a design-token blob, 1 another page's triage decision — and FIVE were items this gate "+
+			"had already BLOCKED one attempt earlier (0ceacd8f, 9ae28ee3, f65a1834, f4003032, a2ef2613)",

edits.rationale: Switch on the outcome. The refusal returns a DISTINCT status from the no-change block because it is a distinct claim, and skips gate 2 for the same reason the existing block arm does: the item is not completing, so there is nothing to grade. The abstain arm is unchanged — gate 2 still runs, because abstaining from ONE gate must not skip the other.

A fifth cause with its own sentence and reason code. This function's whole history is a message that recorded a finding the verifier never made, so reusing the fourth arm's text would be that defect again: there the handler said plainly it changed nothing (a readable payload with zeros in it); here NOTHING was readable, so no gate graded anything. The remedy an operator owes is different — identify the payload's producer, not hunt a defect nobody found.

THE FORCING FUNCTION, extending the guard that already fails an entry with no Why or no CounterPaths rather than adding a new mechanism: an undeclared OnUnreadable is unshippable, and a refusal with no UnreadableWhy is unshippable. Table cases use the LIVE payloads (spawn record from row a2ef2613, foreign triage from 525275da, the existing design-token blob) because a fixture written to exercise a rule will exercise it. withRosterEntry installs synthetic entries so the two abstain declarations — including the zero value — are asserted by something rather than by nothing.

Closes a gap WII-017 records against itself: 'no unit test asserts that verifyBeforeComplete calls the gate (it needs a *sql.DB)'. A pure function returning the right answer into a caller that ignores it is a guard that reads as protection and is not one. Drives verifyBeforeComplete over sqlmock and asserts the CALLER's outputs. THE CONTROLS ARE THE POINT: a readable all-zero payload must still block as handler_reported_no_change, and an un-opted-in item_type must complete with no _verification and no abstention — a gate that refused everything would satisfy the refusal test alone.

Condition (2) of the 2026-07-28 ordering exemption: the seam is registered in the same commit that ships it. Three in-place corrections rather than a new entry, because this AMENDS an existing seam: the abstain-arm LANDMINE is corrected (it is no longer unconditional), the 'wiring proven only behaviourally' gap is marked CLOSED, and the '_verification.status has four values' relation is updated to five. It also records that WII-017's stated expectation — 'a busy NO_CHANGE_GATE_UNREADABLE_RESULT stream is the gate WORKING' — is no longer the steady state post-287.

grounded_in: complete_work_item_verification.go (gate 2, RFC_017): 'verifier errors -> fail CLOSED. Do NOT complete; route into the attempt machinery, exactly as for a persisting defect. "I could not check" is no longer treated as "I checked and it is fixed".'

runRegisteredVerifier, on the unparseable-spec branch: 'Deliberately not exempted: an unparseable spec is if anything MORE suspicious than a verifier's own error, and exempting it would leave a second silent completion path behind the one RFC_017 closed.'

complete_work_item_no_change.go, the arm being changed: 'The item still completes: a payload this guard cannot read is not evidence of a no-op, and inverting that would block legitimate work on a handler whose response shape simply differs.'

complete_work_item_no_change.go header, on what a roster entry means: 'Whoever adds a type here is asserting, for that type, that a zero-change run cannot be a repair — and owes the measurement that says so, in the rule's Why.'
